pages.observation: 0) Looking at the image, I saw no visible difference from the page 08 image I viewed for the earlier request. The hash change may come from non-visual export differences, but I cannot confirm that. 1) The order is mostly clear: the 2+1 rows read naturally left to right. In the bottom tier, the tall left panel (4) comes before the stacked right panels (5, then 6). Some readers may hesitate between 4 and 5. The three notification panels seem to be simultaneous, but no caption says so. 2) There is only one speech balloon (labtech, panel 3), and its tail points correctly to the labtech placeholder. All other figures are silent. Ravi gives no reply or reaction to 'All done, Ravi!', and no reaction to his notification in panel 4. With placeholder art no reaction can be seen. 3) The teal label boxes have no tails and nothing marks what shows them: a screen, a sign or a phone. A reader cannot tell whether 'NEW PRESCRIPTION', 'LAB ORDER: samples to collect', the two 'RESULTS READY' labels and 'Welbuk Health app · email · WhatsApp' are on-screen text or captions. 'RESULTS READY' appears twice with the same wording (panels 5 and 6). In panel 6 the label sits right beside the 'meera' name tag at the panel's right edge. 4) Text fit: in panel 2 ('The lab is notified.') and panel 4 ('Ravi is notified.'), the final period touches or reaches the right border of the caption box, so the text looks like it overflows slightly. In panel 1, 'fills' runs close to the box edge. In panel 3 the balloon shows 'We' ll' with a visible gap after the apostrophe, which looks like a font or kerning problem. 5) Continuity: the page opens with 'Meanwhile', which depends on the previous page. Nobody on this page is shown writing the prescription or ordering the lab work. The jump from sample collection ('Later that day') to 'Results ready' has no caption showing how much time passed. Nothing follows up on the pharmacy prescription. 6) Five captions in a row use the same 'X is notified' wording, so the page reads as a list of notifications rather than a scene. All text was readable and no file was unreadable.
